messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In domestic cats and many wild felids, the presence of a mane (the long, shaggy fur around the head and neck) is controlled by a dominant allele. In lions, the gene responsible for mane development is expressed when at least one copy of the dominant allele is present. Thus, male lions typically have a mane because they inherit the dominant allele from at least one parent, while females do not develop a mane because the allele is recessive in them.
